placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_lasalle, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is NOT a measurement of this frontage either: it is the line the buildings already standing on this face were built to, adopted so that the face carries one street wall rather than two (T-0104). The plat module's lot margin still fixes the side lines this run stands clear of; what it does not fix is a street line that other records had already set, and its west wall is fixed by the east wall of recon_1835_blk_south_water_lasalle_d7_12, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.
placement.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by South Water, Clark, Lake and Lasalle; standing ON the South Water Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 6 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.value: H. Doty & Co. — dry goods and groceries
occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on South Water Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 4 printings, 1834-05-28 to 1834-07-02, claims chicago_democrat_1834_05_28#c008, chicago_democrat_1834_06_04#c021, chicago_democrat_1834_07_02#c010, chicago_democrat_1834_07_02#c057 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF'S PLATTED LOT FACES South Water Street, which is the plat's own answer to which street it fronts. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

citations.citation: The Chicago Democrat. Vol. I, No. 1 (November 26, 1833) through Vol. II, No. 18 (August 26, 1835). Chicago, Ill.: John Calhoun, editor and publisher. Seventy-three issues, OCR-assisted research transcriptions from page scans.
what_it_supplies: that a named trade was being carried on in Chicago in a named week, and often where
self-reported addresses, which are the strongest address evidence this project has: the advertiser was paying, and his customers had to find him
dissolution, removal and replacement notices — the only thing that keeps a documented business out of the 1835 town under the owner's ruling 3
post-office letter lists, naming residents by the hundred (ruling 1: a listed name mints a resident candidate, flagged letter_list_only)
the village and later town ordinances, printed complete — the 7 November 1833 code is the richest single item in the run
arrivals and clearances, which date the piers and the harbour as working structures
public notices that fix a building as a polling place, an auction site or a meeting place on a given day
the paper's own imprint, self-reported: the corner of South Water and Clark streets
twenty-one months of continuous weekly attestation ending three weeks before the scene date, including the issue printed on 1835-07-01
what_it_does_not_supply: any building's form, material, storey count, fenestration or dimensions — an advertisement describes a trade, not a building
the specific corner of any junction it names: 'on the corner of' does not say which of the four
anything at all from an engraving — see trap 1; the cuts are the printer's stock
proof that a business named in 1833 or 1834 still stood on 1835-07-01; that is ruling 3's survival liberty, and it is a liberty
an argument from silence, unless corpus.json shows the issues either side of the silence are both in the deposit
a reading that outranks a scan read of the same passage — see ruling 2 and the C. & I. HARMON case
a citation without an issue page and column

frontage.why: T-0429, and the ground it stands on was unblocked by an owner's ruling rather than found. T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might move, and T-0317 inherited the refusal; T-0009 closed it on 2026-08-29 under the owner's ruling that THE DRAWN SOUTH WATER LINE DOES NOT MOVE — the corridor was re-derived from committed control and data/streets/1835.json was not touched. That refusal is what had held this reach, and it is discharged. THE FACE IS THE BLOCK'S OWN, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: tools/measure_street_frontage.py reads South Water and Lake as the two faces of this block, the committed street hierarchy in data/streets/1835.json grades both `principal`, and South Water is the river street the owner's reference plate draws — 'South Water Street in 1834', roughly ten one-storey log and frame buildings shoulder to shoulder facing the river. This run is the west half of that row on this block. THE LINE IS NOT AUTHORED AT ALL, which is the difference between this run and the first deal's: the face is already built, so the run declares `adopts_face_line` and the 1.5 m is MEASURED off the three units the first deal stands on the same face — 1.4998, 1.4996 and 1.5004 m, a 0.8 mm spread — under T-0104's clause. A street wall is one wall, and this row joins one rather than opening one. THE CORNER CLAUSE BINDS AND THE FABRIC RULE AGREES WITH IT, which is the parcel's one new reading. Lot 0 is the block's free CORNER lot, at South Water and LaSalle, and the core density standard's third clause says a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER: the run is anchored WEST, 1.5 m clear of the corner margin, and chains east on shared party walls. The frontage-fabric rule (T-0022) independently says a log dwelling takes the WEST END of a principal-street row where the block was dealt one, and this block was dealt a D1. On blk_randolph_market (T-0317) the corner clause and the end rule pointed in opposite directions and the parcel had to choose; here the corner clause and the fabric rule name the SAME unit, so the log cabin takes the corner and nothing has to be traded away. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the strip's two ends and the party walls between units are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the lots this run was dealt are named here so the ledger can count them rather than shared out one per unit.
